test.title: Electromagnetic Induction - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: The magnetic field B crossing normally a square metallic plate of area 4 m2 is changing with time as shown in figure. The magnitude of induced emf in the plate during t=2 s to t=4 s, is _____ mV.

A horizontal straight wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> long extending from east to west falling freely at right angle to horizontal component of earth's magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Wb</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The instantaneous value of emf induced in the wire when its velocity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>.

A circular coil of 1000 turns each with area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is rotated about its vertical diameter at the rate of one revolution per second in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>07</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The maximum voltage generation will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>.

The current in an inductor is given by $\mathrm{I}=(3 \mathrm{t}+8)$ where $\mathrm{t}$ is in second. The magnitude of induced emf produced in the inductor is $12 \mathrm{mV}$. The self-inductance of the inductor _____ $\mathrm{mH}$.

Three identical resistors with resistance R=12 Ω and two identical inductors with sell inductance L=5 mH are connected to an ideal battery with emf of 12 V as shown in figure. The current through the battery long after the switch has been closed will be________A.

A coil has an inductance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> and resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is applied across the coil. The energy stored in the magnetic field after the current has built up to its equilibrium value will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>

A circular conducting coil of radius 1 m is being heated by the change of magnetic field B→ passing perpendicular to the plane in which the coil is laid. The resistance of the coil is 2 μΩ. The magnetic field is slowly switched off such that its magnitude changes in time as  

B=4π×10-3 T1-t100

The energy dissipated by the coil before the magnetic field is switched off completely is E=______mJ.

A conducting bar moves on two conducting rails as shown in the figure. A constant magnetic field B exists into the page. The bar starts to move from the vertex at time $t=0$ with a constant velocity. If the induced EMF is $\mathrm{E} \propto \mathrm{t}^{\mathrm{n}}$, then value of n is _.

Two coils have mutual inductance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>002</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math>. The current changes in the first coil according to the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mi>π</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The maximum value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>emf</mi></math> in the second coil is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi>α</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is

A square shaped coil of area 70 cm2 having 600 turns rotates in a magnetic field of 0.4 Wb m–2, about an axis which is parallel to one of the side of the coil and perpendicular to the direction of field. If the coil completes 500 revolution in a minute, the instantaneous emf when the plane of the coil is inclined at 60° with the field, will be ______ V.

(Take π=227)

In the given figure, an inductor and resistor are connected in series with a battery of emf E volt. Ea2b J s-1 represents the maximum rate at which the energy is stored in the magnetic field (inductor). The numerical value of ba will be _____.
As per the given figure, if dIdt=-1 A s-1, then the value of VAB at this instant will be ______ V.

Two concentric circular coils, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, are placed in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi><mi>Y</mi></math> plane. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn></math>turns, and a radius of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> has 200 turns and radius of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mtext>.</mtext><mo> </mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> carries a time dependent current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi><mfenced><mi mathvariant="italic">t</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is in s. The emf induced in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mfenced><mrow><mi>in</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mV</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> at the instant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>s is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ..........

A square loop PQRS having 10 turns, area $3.6 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2$ and resistance $100 \Omega$ is slowly and uniformly being pulled out of a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $\mathrm{B}=0.5 \mathrm{~T}$ as shown. Work done in pulling the loop out of the field in $1.0 \mathrm{~s}$ is ______ $\times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}$.

When a coil is connected across a $20 \mathrm{~V}$ dc supply, it draws a current of $5 \mathrm{~A}$. When it is connected across $20 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}$ ac supply, it draws a current of $4 \mathrm{~A}$. The self inductance of the coil is ______ $\mathrm{mH}$. $($ Take $\pi=3$ )

A circular coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is placed in a uniform magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> with its plane perpendicular to the field initially. It is rotated at constant angular speed about an axis along the diameter of coil and perpendicular to magnetic field so that it undergoes half of rotation in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The maximum value of EMF induced (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>μV</mi></math>) in the coil will be close to the integer....

A circular coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> turns is rotated about its vertical diameter with an angular speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The maximum emf induced in the coil will be _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> volt (rounded off to the nearest integer).

A small square loop of wire of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>l</mi></math> is placed inside a large square loop of wire of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>. The loops are coplanar and their centers coincide. The value of the mutual inductance of the system is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math>______.

Magnetic flux (in weber) in a closed circuit of resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> varies with time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mfenced><mi>s</mi></mfenced></math> as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The magnitude of the induced current at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mA</mi></math>.

Conductor wire ABCDE with each $\operatorname{arm} 10 \mathrm{~cm}$ in length is placed in magnetic field of $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ Tesla, perpendicular to its plane. When conductor is pulled towards right with constant velocity of $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$, induced emf between points A and E is _____ mV.
